title: Set 137

sentences.ko: 한 달쯤 도자기에 완전히 빠져서 도구까지 전부 샀거든. 근데 수업이 끝나고 다른 수업을 못 찾아서, 지금은 그게 다 차고에 있는 상자 안에 그냥 처박혀 있어. 그때 바로 다음 수업을 신청했으면 아마 아직도 하고 있을 거야.
sentences.text: I got really into pottery for like a month, I even bought all the tools, but then the class ended and I never found another one, so now it's all just sitting in a box in the garage. I think if I'd signed up for the next class right away, I'd probably still be doing it.

alts.text: Pottery was my thing for like a month. Bought all the tools and everything, but the class ended and I couldn't find another one, so now it's all just sitting in a box in the garage. If I'd signed up for the next class right away, I'd probably still be at it.

I became very interested in pottery for about a month, and I even purchased all of the tools. However, the class ended and I was unable to find another one, so everything is now sitting in a box in the garage. I believe that if I had enrolled in the next class immediately, I would most likely still be doing it.

sentences.note: **got really into** 는 무언가에 푹 빠졌다는 뜻이에요. **sitting in a box** 는 물건이 쓰이지 않고 상자 안에 방치돼 있다는 느낌을 줍니다.

sentences.ko: 우리 토요일마다 가던 모퉁이 빵집 기억나? 주인이 바뀌었는데 빵이 예전 같지 않아, 좀 퍽퍽해졌어. 그래서 이제 안 가는데 아쉬워. 솔직히 그 길을 걷는 게 좋았던 이유가 그 빵집 하나뿐이었거든.
sentences.text: Remember that bakery on the corner we used to go to every Saturday? They got new owners, and the bread just isn't the same anymore, it's kind of dry now. So I stopped going, which is a shame, because it was honestly the only reason I liked walking down that street.

alts.text: You know that corner bakery we'd hit every Saturday? New owners now, and the bread's just not the same, it's kinda dry. So I quit going, which sucks, 'cause honestly it was the only reason I liked walking down that street.

Do you remember the bakery on the corner that we used to visit every Saturday? It has new owners, and the bread is simply not the same anymore; it is rather dry now. I therefore stopped going, which is unfortunate, because it was truly the only reason I enjoyed walking down that street.

sentences.note: **isn't the same anymore** 는 예전 같지 않다, 변했다는 뜻이에요. **which is a shame** 은 앞에 한 말을 받아 그게 아쉽다고 덧붙일 때 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 알았어, 요리 프로그램 같이 볼게. 대신 딱 한 편만 보고 끄는 거야. 너는 맨날 한 편만 더 하다가 정신 차려 보면 새벽 두 시잖아. 콜?
sentences.text: Okay, I'll watch the cooking show with you, but only if we stop after one episode, because you always say just one more and then suddenly it's two in the morning. Deal?

alts.text: Fine, I'll watch the cooking show with you, but just one episode, 'cause you always go just one more and next thing you know it's two a.m. Deal?

Very well, I will watch the cooking show with you, but only on the condition that we stop after one episode, because you always say just one more, and then suddenly it is two in the morning. Do we have an agreement?

sentences.note: **but only if** 는 ~라는 조건이면 해 줄게라는 뜻이에요. **Deal?** 은 이 조건으로 하는 거지? 하고 확인할 때 짧게 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 시내 커피숍이 전부 꽉 차서 한 네 군데는 돌아다녔는데, 겨우 자리를 잡았을 때는 커피 생각이 아예 없어졌어. 그냥 테이크아웃해서 공원에 앉아 있을 걸 그랬어.
sentences.text: Every coffee place downtown was packed, so we ended up trying like four different spots, and by the time we finally found a table I didn't even want coffee anymore. We should've just gotten it to go and sat in the park.

alts.text: All the coffee places downtown were packed, so we hit like four different spots, and by the time we got a table I didn't even want coffee anymore. Shoulda just grabbed it to go and sat in the park.

Every coffee shop downtown was crowded, so we ended up trying approximately four different places, and by the time we finally found a table, I no longer wanted coffee. We should have simply ordered it to go and sat in the park.

sentences.note: **ended up** 은 어쩌다 보니 결국 ~하게 됐다는 뜻이에요. **should've just gotten it to go** 는 그냥 포장해 올 걸 그랬다는 후회입니다.

sentences.ko: 응, 다 괜찮아요, 아빠. 차요? 차도 잘 굴러가요. 음, 소리가 좀 나긴 하는데 목요일에 정비 맡길 거니까 걱정 안 하셔도 돼요, 알았죠?
sentences.text: Yeah, everything's fine, Dad. The car? It's running great. Well, it's making a little noise, but I'm taking it in on Thursday, so you don't need to worry about it, okay?

alts.text: It's all good, Dad. The car? Runs great. Okay, it's making a little noise, but I'm taking it in Thursday, so don't worry about it, okay?

Yes, everything is fine, Dad. The car? It is running very well. Admittedly, it is making a slight noise, but I am taking it in for service on Thursday, so there is no need for you to worry about it, all right?

sentences.note: **taking it in** 은 차를 정비소에 맡긴다는 뜻이에요. **running great** 는 차가 문제없이 잘 굴러간다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기
